correctness.rationale: Coefficient matching proves semisymmetry iff A^3=-I and c in ker(A+I). The commuting fraction q^(-r) follows from A-A^(-1)=A(A+I). Each conjugacy-class formula follows from split factors, degree-two irreducible factor, or the three Jordan block multiplicities in characteristic three. With gamma_infty(q)>0, centralizer sums are uniformly comparable to a fixed discrete Gaussian exp(-3(r-r_n)^2/2), including the characteristic-three allowed rank boundary. Thus total counts and the q^(-2n/3) weighted mean follow. The 14-stratum checker plus 7 direct operation checks passed; finite tests are supplementary, not proofs of the infinite theorem.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The published matrix-class and cubic-identity lemmas are deliberately incorporated as premises, not presented as independent novelty. Their conjunction with the commuting-pair count yields a formula after analysis, while the unconditional quasigroup existence theorem provides no lower or upper measure bound on the specified subclass. The new asymptotic requires optimizing a three-sector conjugacy-count exponent and controlling all ranks uniformly, including inseparable characteristic three.

evidence: Allsop–Wanless enumerates allowed values of number of commuting pairs, not counts of affine semisymmetric operators by value.
Smith–Wang gives no dimension-parametric rank-conditioned commuting census in the inspected section.
The finite-dimensional identities were independently recomputed in 14 exhaustive matrix configurations; their mere agreement does not establish originality.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No inspected exact table is equivalent to the entire parameterized weighted distribution. The finite-field centralizer components by themselves are known and not claimed as the original part.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the conditioned rank-weighted commuting-pair distribution and fixed-q dimension-asymptotic concentration across all characteristics. Allsop–Wanless covers the unrestricted existence spectrum, Smith–Wang covers the cubic linear criterion, and the known Kung–Stong/Fulman matrix cycle index covers conjugacy centralizers, but none of the inspected corresponding scientific statements supplies the complete conditioned distribution or its two-thirds law. Searching cannot prove absence, and equivalent unindexed work remains a risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent conditional quasigroup census or two-thirds asymptotic could exist in unindexed literature, including algebraic-combinatorial studies of medial or central quasigroups.
Matrix centralizer formulas are classical and directly yield part of the finite formula; novelty is asserted only for the quasigroup interpretation plus the conditioned probabilistic asymptotic.
The potentially relevant Kozlik 2026 manuscript was not read in full, so no full-text exclusion is claimed.
This assessment is not independent external validation.

value.rationale: Allsop–Wanless highlights commuting-pair spectra and suggests more structured quasigroup subclasses. The present result determines the complete conditioned distribution for a natural semisymmetric affine subfamily, quantifies its characteristic-specific support and establishes field-uniform-in-dimension concentration with the same two-thirds exponent across three distinct rational-canonical regimes. Exact self-contained quantities for every n and q support future probabilistic classification; the result is not limited to an arbitrary finite table or a restatement of general matrix centralizers.
